title: Organic Synthesis
tagline: Retrosynthesis, determining mechanisms, oxidation and reduction, protecting groups, C–C bond formation, pericyclic reactions, stereoselectivity and total synthesis
summary: Synthesis is the art of making molecules by design. This course teaches retrosynthetic planning and the evidence used to establish mechanisms, then the main tools of the synthetic chemist — selective oxidation and reduction, protecting groups, carbon–carbon bond formation, pericyclic reactions and stereoselective methods — and studies how they come together in total synthesis.

chapters.title: Retrosynthetic analysis
chapters.summary: Disconnections and synthons, functional-group interconversion, and choosing between routes.

chapters.title: Determining reaction mechanisms
chapters.summary: Kinetic evidence, isotope labelling and isotope effects, Hammett correlations, trapping intermediates and stereochemical probes.

chapters.title: Oxidation and reduction in synthesis
chapters.summary: Chemoselective oxidants and reductants, and choosing reagents for functional-group interconversions.

chapters.title: Protecting groups
chapters.summary: Protecting alcohols, amines and carbonyl groups, and orthogonal protection strategies.

chapters.title: Forming carbon–carbon bonds
chapters.summary: Organometallic additions, the Wittig reaction and related olefinations, enolate chemistry and cross-coupling in synthesis.

chapters.title: Pericyclic reactions
chapters.summary: Cycloadditions such as the Diels–Alder reaction, electrocyclic reactions and sigmatropic rearrangements, and the Woodward–Hoffmann rules.

chapters.title: Stereoselective synthesis
chapters.summary: Diastereoselective reactions and the Felkin–Anh model, the chiral pool, chiral auxiliaries and asymmetric catalysis.

chapters.title: Rearrangements, carbenes and radicals in synthesis
chapters.summary: Cationic rearrangements, carbenes and nitrenes, and radical cyclisations as synthetic tools.

chapters.title: Strategy in total synthesis
chapters.summary: Convergent and linear strategies, step economy, and case studies of landmark syntheses of natural products.
